column1: One row per status. Abilities apply these by id through status_apply / status_duration. Add a status by adding a row and teaching Kinds what reads it.

column6: *2* of your broken {LAYERS} are being held down. They stay broken until this wears off.
column20: Holds this many broken layers down: they stay broken while it lasts.

column6: At the end of every round one of your own attacks is turned *on yourself*.
column20: Each round end the victim turns one of its OWN attacks on itself.

column6: Your {EC} is over your {MS}. Your line is being invaded until you burn it down.
column20: DERIVED, not timed: it lasts while ec > ms, so it is never stored in unit.statuses.

column6: {ANGER} has blotted out your aim. *Half* of your attacks miss outright.
column20: The victim fluffs this fraction of its attacks.

column6: {SURPRISE} came from nowhere. *A third* of your attacks go wide.
column20: Surprise's own miss status. missChance() takes the HIGHEST of everything on a unit rather than summing, so Rattled and Blinded together are just Blinded.

column6: You cannot keep anything down. *Two in five* of your attacks go wide, and one of them comes back at *you* every round.
column20: TWO levers at once, which is what makes it the priciest debuff in the game: it is Blinded and Sad in a single slot, a little weaker at each than either is alone.

column6: *3* of your broken {LAYERS} are being held down, and nothing is going your way.
column20: The only status that moves crit odds. -0.045 against a base critChance of 0.05 leaves half a percent - not quite never, which is worse to play against than never.

column6: The carriage is still moving without you. *Half* of your attacks miss outright.
column20: Blinded's miss rate for a SINGLE turn - what Drug Hit leaves behind. The whole difference between this and BLINDED is how long you live with it, which is what makes a one-turn status worth costing as a basic attack rather than as a debuff.
